questions.question: ​What was the primary purpose of the Mansabdari system under Akbar?

options.text: To establish control over the southern kingdoms.
To organize the military and nobility for efficient administration.
To encourage the formation of private armies.
To facilitate foreign trade and commerce.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To organize the military and nobility for efficient administration.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was introduced by **Akbar** in the Mughal Empire to establish a centralized and efficient administrative structure for both military and civil governance.
 
• The term **"Mansab"** refers to "rank" or "position," and it determined the status, salary, and number of troops a Mansabdar (rank-holder) was required to maintain for the empire.
 
• The system categorized Mansabdars into grades, ranging from **10 to 10,000**, based on their rank, with higher ranks commanding larger numbers of troops and receiving higher salaries.
 
• The primary purpose of the Mansabdari system was to create a structured and organized military force that was directly controlled by the emperor, ensuring loyalty and reducing the power of regional governors and nobles.
 
• The Mansabdari system also served as an administrative tool to manage the vast Mughal Empire, as Mansabdars were often assigned both military and civil responsibilities in their designated territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ranking System:**

 
 
• The Mansabdari system was divided into two ranks - **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• The **Zat rank** determined the individual's personal status and salary.
 
• The **Sawar rank** indicated the number of cavalrymen a Mansabdar was required to maintain and provide during wartime.
 
 
 
• **Recruitment and Payment:**
 
 
• Mansabdars were primarily recruited based on merit, loyalty, and lineage.
 
• Their salaries were often paid through the assignment of **Jagirs (land revenue)**, though the revenue was collected by the state and then distributed to the Mansabdars.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Importance:**
 
 
• The Mansabdari system ensured that the Mughal emperor had a **well-disciplined and efficient military force**.
 
• It also centralized power in the hands of the emperor, reducing the autonomy of provincial rulers.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the System:**
 
 
• Over time, the Mansabdari system became corrupt, with Mansabdars often misreporting troop numbers or embezzling funds.
 
• The inability to maintain the system efficiently was one of the factors contributing to the decline of the Mughal Empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Mansabdari system was inspired by the **Persian administrative and military practices** and adapted to suit the needs of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It played a crucial role in consolidating Akbar’s rule over a vast and diverse empire.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Systems:**
 
 
• The Mansabdari system was unique compared to earlier systems like the **Iqtadari system** used during the Delhi Sultanate, as it combined both military and civil administration under centralized control.
 
• It also differed from the feudal systems in Europe, as Mansabdars were not hereditary lords but appointed officials under the emperor's command.

questions.question: The hormone that is present in greater concentrations in fruits and seeds is ________.
questions.solution:
__**Correct Answer: Cytokinin**__

__**Rationale**__:

__
 
• Cytokinins are a class of plant hormones that promote cell division, or cytokinesis, in plant roots and shoots. They are present in greater concentrations in fruits and seeds, playing a critical role in their development and growth.
 
• These hormones are essential for various aspects of plant growth and development, including the stimulation of cell division, the promotion of shoot initiation and growth, and the delay of leaf senescence.
 
• Cytokinins also work in conjunction with other plant hormones such as auxins to regulate various physiological processes, including nutrient mobilization and the formation of chloroplasts in leaves.

**Explanation of Other Options:**__

**Auxin**

 
• Rationale: Auxins are another class of plant hormones that are primarily involved in the elongation of cells in stems, root growth, and the differentiation of cells. They are not present in greater concentrations in fruits and seeds compared to cytokinins.

**Gibberellin**

 
• Rationale: Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering. While they play significant roles in plant development, their concentration in fruits and seeds is not as high as that of cytokinins.

**ABA (Abscisic Acid)**

 
• Rationale: Abscisic Acid (ABA) is a plant hormone that primarily functions in stress responses, such as promoting stomatal closure during drought conditions. It also plays a role in seed dormancy. ABA is not present in greater concentrations in fruits and seeds compared to cytokinins.

**Conclusion**:

 
• Among the given options, cytokinins are the plant hormones present in greater concentrations in fruits and seeds. They are vital for promoting cell division, delaying leaf senescence, and working with other hormones to regulate various growth processes in plants.

questions.question: Which of the following Union Territories has a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Puducherry** (formerly known as **Pondicherry**) is a **Union Territory** that possesses its own **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** to assist and advise the **Lieutenant Governor**. This provision was enabled by the **14th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962**, which inserted **Article 239A** into the **Constitution of India**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Puducherry having a legislature is correct.***
 
• The **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963** provides the framework for the **Legislative Assembly** of **Puducherry**. Currently, the assembly consists of **33 members**, out of which **30 are directly elected** by the people and **3 are nominated** by the **Central Government**.
 
• **Daman and Diu** and **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** were previously separate **Union Territories** without their own legislatures. They were merged into a single entity known as the **Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu** on **January 26, 2020**. This combined territory is administered directly by the **President** through an **Administrator** and does not have a **Legislative Assembly**. ***Hence, the statement regarding these territories having a legislature is incorrect.***
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** is an island territory located in the **Bay of Bengal**. It is categorized as a **Union Territory** without a legislature and is administered by a **Lieutenant Governor** appointed by the **President of India**. Decisions for the islands are made through the **Home Ministry** and the **Presidential** regulations under **Article 240**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Andaman and Nicobar Islands having a legislature is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Union Territories:** **Part VIII** of the **Constitution of India** (**Articles 239 to 241**) deals with the administration of **Union Territories**. While some **UTs** are directly administered by the **President** through an **Administrator**, others like **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, and **Jammu & Kashmir** have been provided with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** due to their specific administrative and political needs.
 
• **The Case of Delhi:** The **National Capital Territory of Delhi** was provided with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** through the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991**, which added **Article 239AA**. Unlike **Puducherry**, **Delhi's** assembly has restricted powers over subjects like **Public Order**, **Police**, and **Land**, which remain under the **Central Government**.
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization:** Following the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019**, the former state was bifurcated into two **Union Territories**: **Jammu & Kashmir** (with a legislature) and **Ladakh** (without a legislature). This change came into effect on **October 31, 2019**.
 
• **Difference in Administration:** In **Union Territories** like **Chandigarh** or **Lakshadweep**, the **Administrator** (often an **IAS officer** or a political appointee) holds the executive power. In **UTs** with a legislature, the **Lieutenant Governor** (**LG**) acts as the **Constitutional Head**, but the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister** exercises executive powers on most state subjects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legislative Scope:** The **Legislative Assembly** of **Puducherry** can make laws on any subject mentioned in the **State List** or the **Concurrent List** of the **Seventh Schedule**, provided those laws do not conflict with laws made by the **Parliament**.
 
• **Role of the President:** Under **Article 240**, the **President of India** has the power to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of certain **Union Territories**. However, for **Puducherry**, this power can only be exercised when the **Assembly** is dissolved or suspended.
 
• **Current Status:** As of **2024**, India has **8 Union Territories**. Out of these, only **3** (**Delhi**, **Puducherry**, and **Jammu & Kashmir**) are constitutionally designated to have their own **Legislative Assemblies**. The remaining **5** (**Chandigarh**, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**, **Lakshadweep**, **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, and **Ladakh**) do not have a local legislature.

questions.question: In water, the ratio of oxygen to hydrogen by mass is
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __8:1__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Chemical Composition of Water__**

 __
 
• The chemical formula for water is **H₂O__**, indicating it consists of two atoms of **__Hydrogen__** and one atom of **__Oxygen__**.
 
• To find the ratio by mass, the atomic masses of the constituent elements must be considered:
 __
 
• The **atomic mass__** of Hydrogen (H) is approximately **__1 unit__**.
 
• The **__atomic mass__** of Oxygen (O) is approximately **__16 units__**.
 
 
 
• Calculation of mass in one molecule:
 __
 
• Total mass of Hydrogen = 2 atoms × 1 = **2 units__**.
 
• Total mass of Oxygen = 1 atom × 16 = **__16 units__**.
 
 
 
• The ratio of **__Oxygen to Hydrogen__** by mass is 16 : 2, which simplifies to **__8 : 1__**.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Law of Constant Proportions__**

 __
 
• Also known as **Proust's Law__**, it states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a **__fixed ratio__** by mass, regardless of its source or method of preparation.
 
• Water, whether from a river or a laboratory, will always maintain the **__8 : 1__** mass ratio of oxygen to hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **__Molecular Mass__**
 __
 
• The total **molecular mass__** of water (H₂O) is approximately **__18 units__** (2 from hydrogen + 16 from oxygen).
 
• In terms of percentage, water is roughly **__88.8% oxygen__** and **__11.2% hydrogen__** by mass.
 
 
 
• **__Ratio by Volume__**
 __
 
• While the ratio by mass is 8:1, the **ratio by volume__** (or molar ratio) of hydrogen to oxygen gas produced during the electrolysis of water is **__2 : 1__**.

questions.question: Which Article deals with the constitution of Municipalities?

• Municipalities are empowered to carry out functions related to urban development, including planning, infrastructure, sanitation, and public amenities.
 
• This Article forms part of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which aimed to strengthen decentralized governance in urban areas.
 
• It ensures democratic representation in municipalities through elected representatives, promoting grassroots democracy and efficient urban administration.

• This Article specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities.
 
• It empowers municipalities to prepare plans for economic development and social justice, along with the implementation of schemes related to 18 functional areas listed in the Twelfth Schedule.
 
• Key functions include urban planning, water supply, sanitation, public health, urban forestry, slum improvement, and poverty alleviation.
 
 
 
• **Article 243Z:**
 
 
• This Article focuses on the audit and accounts of municipalities.
 
• It ensures financial accountability by mandating regular audits of municipal accounts by the State Government or an authorized agency.
 
• The Article aims to enhance transparency and efficiency in the management of municipal resources.

questions.question: Which blood vessels carry oxygenated blood from the heart to all parts of the body in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Artery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arteries** are the blood vessels that carry **oxygenated blood** away from the heart to all parts of the body.
 
• The **pulmonary arteries** are an exception as they carry **deoxygenated blood** from the heart to the lungs.
 
• The oxygen-rich blood is pumped by the heart's left ventricle into the **aorta**, the largest artery, which branches out into smaller arteries and delivers oxygen to tissues.
 
• Arteries have **thick, elastic walls** to withstand the high pressure of blood being pumped by the heart.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining the **circulatory system** and ensuring that all body tissues receive oxygen and nutrients for proper functioning.
 
• Arteries also help regulate blood pressure through the elasticity of their walls, which can expand and contract based on the body's requirements.
 
• Veins, venules, and capillaries serve different purposes and do not carry oxygenated blood from the heart to the body tissues. Hence, the correct answer is Artery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Veins:**

 
 
• Veins carry **deoxygenated blood** back to the heart, except for the pulmonary veins, which carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
 
• They have **thin walls** and are equipped with **valves** to prevent backflow of blood.
 
 
 
• **Venules:**
 
 
• Venules are small blood vessels that collect blood from capillaries and transport it to veins.
 
• They play a role in connecting the capillaries to the larger veins.
 
 
 
• **Capillaries:**
 
 
• Capillaries are the **smallest blood vessels** where the exchange of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and waste products occurs between blood and tissues.
 
• They connect arteries and veins and have **thin walls** to facilitate diffusion of substances.
 
 
 
• **Function of Arteries:**
 
 
• Arteries ensure the supply of oxygenated blood to vital organs, maintaining their proper functioning.
 
• Examples include the **coronary arteries** (supplying the heart), **renal arteries** (supplying the kidneys), and **carotid arteries** (supplying the brain).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Arteries:**

 
 
• Arteries have **thicker walls** compared to veins to handle the high pressure of blood flow.
 
• The blood in arteries flows in **one direction**, from the heart to the body tissues.
 
 
 
• **Differences between Arteries and Veins:**
 
 
• Arteries carry oxygenated blood, while veins carry deoxygenated blood (with exceptions for pulmonary arteries and veins).
 
• Arteries have no valves, while veins have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.
 
• Arteries are located deeper in the body, whereas veins are closer to the skin.

questions.question: The total length of the Northern Plain of India from west to east is approximately ______.

• The Northern Plain of India spans approximately **2400 km** in length from west to east, extending through the states of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by three major river systems: **the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra**.
 
• It is one of the world's most fertile regions and forms a significant part of the **Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain**.
 
• The plain is broadly divided into three sections: the Punjab Plains in the west, the Ganga Plains in the center, and the Brahmaputra Plains in the east.
 
• This region is characterized by alluvial soil, making it ideal for agriculture, and it supports a dense population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is rich in nutrients such as potash, phosphoric acid, and lime, making it highly fertile.
 
• The soil supports the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers, along with their tributaries, play a crucial role in shaping the plain.
 
• These rivers provide water for irrigation and contribute to the alluvial deposits.
 
 
 
• **Physiographic Divisions of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Northern Plain is divided into the Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, and Khadar regions based on their geological characteristics.
 
• Khadar (new alluvium) is the most fertile and is renewed annually by river floods.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**

• It is also home to major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow, making it a hub for trade and commerce.

questions.question: Which sector witnessed the slowest growth during the period 1947 to 1991?

__
 
• **Slow Growth in Agricultural Sector:** During the period from **1947 to 1991**, the agricultural sector in India witnessed the slowest growth compared to other sectors. This was primarily due to the lack of modern farming techniques, inadequate irrigation facilities, and dependence on monsoon rains.
 
• **Challenges in Agriculture:** Problems such as fragmented landholdings, low productivity, and insufficient investment in agricultural infrastructure contributed to the slow growth of the sector. Additionally, the Green Revolution of the 1960s only benefited certain regions and crops, leaving other areas stagnant. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• **Focus on Industrial and Service Sectors:** During this period, the Indian government prioritized industrialization and the development of services over agriculture. Policies such as the introduction of heavy industries and economic reforms shifted the focus away from the agricultural sector.
 
• **Low Investment:** Investment in agricultural research, mechanization, and rural infrastructure was limited compared to other sectors. As a result, growth in agriculture lagged behind industrial and service sectors.
 
• **Dependence on Traditional Farming:** Farmers continued to rely on traditional methods of cultivation, which were less efficient and resulted in lower yields. The lack of access to modern technology and fertilizers further hampered growth. *Hence, the correct answer is Agricultural Sector.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Industrial Sector:** Grew rapidly due to policies promoting heavy industries, such as the establishment of steel plants in Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur. The Industrial Policy of 1956 emphasized state-led industrialization.
 
• **Service Sector:** Experienced substantial growth, especially in banking, education, and healthcare sectors. Government initiatives like the nationalization of banks in 1969 contributed to the expansion of services.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Sector Characteristics:**
 
 
• The sector relied heavily on the monsoon for irrigation, making it vulnerable to climatic conditions.
 
• Mechanization was minimal, and the use of modern farming techniques was limited to a few regions benefiting from the Green Revolution.
 
• Despite being the primary source of livelihood for a large population, the agricultural sector did not receive adequate financial or policy support during the period.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution, introduced in the 1960s, improved productivity for crops like wheat and rice but failed to address regional disparities. States like Punjab and Haryana benefited significantly, while others remained underdeveloped.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Policies:**

 
 
• The **Five-Year Plans** aimed at improving agricultural productivity, but the focus remained on industrial growth. For instance, the Second Five-Year Plan emphasized heavy industries over agriculture.
 
• Agriculture was often seen as a traditional sector, leading to lower priority in policy-making compared to industrial and service sectors.
 
 
 
• **Data and Statistics:**
 
 
• According to historical data, agricultural growth rates during this period were often below 2%, while industrial and service sectors achieved higher growth rates, exceeding 5% annually.
 
• The contribution of agriculture to GDP declined significantly from **50% in 1947** to around **30% by 1991**, highlighting its slow growth.

questions.question: Which act replaced FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) in 1999 to facilitate external trade and payments?

options.text: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) was enacted in 1999 and came into effect on **1 June 2000**, replacing the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), 1973.
 
• FEMA was introduced to **facilitate external trade and payments** and to promote the orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market in India.
 
• Unlike FERA, which was stringent and regulatory, FEMA is a **more liberal and market-driven law** designed to simplify foreign exchange management.
 
• FEMA applies to all transactions involving foreign exchange, including **current account transactions, capital account transactions, and dealings in foreign exchange** and securities.
 
• The act is administered by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) under the Ministry of Finance.
 
• The scope of FEMA extends to **Indian citizens, companies, and branches established outside India**, thereby ensuring comprehensive coverage of foreign exchange activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act):**

 
 
• The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 to **prevent monopolistic, restrictive, and unfair trade practices**.
 
• It aimed to curb practices that adversely affected competition in the market.
 
• The Act was replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**, which focuses on promoting competition and preventing anti-competitive practices.
 
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Act, 1992:**
 
 
• This Act established the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** as the regulatory authority for the securities market in India.
 
• It aims to **protect investor interests**, promote the development of the securities market, and regulate its functioning.
 
• SEBI ensures transparency and accountability in the securities market.
 
 
 
• **Banking Regulation Act, 1949:**
 
 
• The Banking Regulation Act provides a framework for the regulation and supervision of banks in India.
 
• It empowers the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to issue licenses to banks, regulate their operations, and oversee mergers and closures.
 
• The act ensures the stability and efficiency of the Indian banking system.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme - Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA):**
 
 
• FEMA was introduced to replace the rigid FERA and align India’s foreign exchange regulations with the **liberalized economic policies** adopted in the 1990s.
 
• It recognizes the importance of foreign exchange in boosting international trade and investment.
 
• FEMA simplifies compliance for businesses, making it easier to engage in cross-border transactions.

__
 
• **42nd Amendment** of the **Indian Constitution**, enacted in **1976**, is known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its extensive changes.
 
• This amendment added the words **‘Socialist’** and **‘Secular’** to the **Preamble** of the Constitution, emphasizing the principles of social justice and secularism in India.
 
• It also introduced the word **‘Integrity’** to stress the importance of national unity and integrity.
 
• The amendment was brought under the leadership of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** during the period of Emergency (1975–1977).
 
• The inclusion of ‘Socialist’ reflects the commitment to eliminating inequalities in income, status, and opportunities, and emphasizes the distribution of wealth for the welfare of all citizens.
 
• The addition of ‘Secular’ underlines that India has no official religion and guarantees freedom of religion to all citizens, along with equality irrespective of religious beliefs.
 
• This amendment brought significant changes to various parts of the Constitution, including strengthening the position of the Directive Principles of State Policy over Fundamental Rights.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 42nd Amendment.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Preamble of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The **Preamble** is the introductory statement of the Constitution, stating its philosophy and objectives.
 
• Originally, the Preamble described India as a **Sovereign Democratic Republic**. The 42nd Amendment added the terms **‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’,** and **‘Integrity’** to expand its scope.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act of 1976:**
 
 
• This amendment is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the structure and functioning of the government.
 
• It made changes to **Articles 31C, 368, and added Article 39A**, focusing on the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It also curtailed the powers of the judiciary and increased the powers of the Parliament and the executive.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Socialist and Secular terms:**
 
 
• **Socialist:** Reflects the government’s commitment to equitable distribution of resources and elimination of social and economic inequalities.
 
• **Secular:** Ensures that India has no official religion and guarantees religious freedom and equality for all its citizens.

• **Key Developments:**

 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** was enacted during the Emergency period (1975–1977), a time marked by controversial decisions under the leadership of **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• It significantly altered the balance of power between the judiciary, legislature, and executive.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• **1976:** The amendment was introduced to align the Constitution with the government’s socialist policies and secular vision during the Emergency.
 
• **Judicial Review:** Many provisions of the amendment were later reviewed and altered by the judiciary in landmark cases such as the **Minerva Mills case (1980).**

questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates system software from application software?

options.text: Application software provides a platform for other software
Both are interchangeable and serve the same purpose.
System software is used for end-user tasks like creating documents
System software provides a platform for other software, while application software allows users to perform specific tasks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**System software provides a platform for other software, while application software allows users to perform specific tasks**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System software** acts as the backbone of a computer, managing hardware and providing a platform for application software to run.
 
• Examples of system software include operating systems like **Windows, macOS, Linux**, and utility programs.
 
• **Application software**, on the other hand, is designed for end-users to perform specific tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, or multimedia editing.
 
• Examples of application software include **Microsoft Word, Excel, Photoshop**, and web browsers like Chrome or Firefox.
 
• The distinction lies in their purpose: system software supports the system's functionality, while application software caters to user-specific needs.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of System Software:**

 
 
• **Operating Systems:** Manage hardware, software resources, and provide services for application software. Examples include Windows and Linux.
 
• **Utility Programs:** Perform maintenance tasks such as antivirus scanning, disk cleanup, and file management.
 
• **Device Drivers:** Enable communication between the operating system and hardware devices like printers and graphics cards.
 
 
 
• **Types of Application Software:**
 
 
• **Productivity Software:** Applications like Microsoft Office Suite for document creation, data analysis, and presentations.
 
• **Entertainment Software:** Games, music players, and video streaming apps.
 
• **Educational Software:** Learning platforms, e-books, and language learning apps.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences:**
 
 
• System software runs in the background and is essential for the system's operation, whereas application software is optional and user-initiated.
 
• System software interacts directly with hardware, while application software interacts with system software for functionality.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• System software is pre-installed on most devices, while application software is often installed based on user requirements.
 
• Both types of software are crucial, but their roles and functionalities differ significantly.

questions.question: Which one of the following dimensions is not included in Human Development Index ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *__** Mortality rate.**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index that measures a country's average achievements in three basic aspects of human development: **health, education, and standard of living.**
 
• The **health dimension** is measured by **Life Expectancy at birth**, which indicates the average number of years a newborn is expected to live assuming that current mortality rates continue to apply.
 
• The **education dimension** is assessed using two indicators: **Mean years of schooling**, which reflects the average number of years of education received by people aged 25 and older, and **Expected years of schooling**, which estimates the total number of years of schooling that a child of school entrance age can expect to receive.
 
• The **standard of living dimension** is measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, which reflects the average income of a country's citizens.
 
• The **Mortality rate** is not included in the HDI. While it is an important indicator of health, it is not directly used in the calculation of HDI. The focus is instead on life expectancy to provide a more comprehensive measure of health and longevity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** was introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its **Human Development Report (HDR)** in **1990**.
 
• The HDI aims to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies. It emphasizes that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country, not economic growth alone.
 
• The three dimensions of HDI are calculated as follows:
 
 
• **Life Expectancy Index**: (Life Expectancy at birth - Minimum value) / (Maximum value - Minimum value)
 
• **Education Index**: (Mean years of schooling index + Expected years of schooling index) / 2
 
• **Income Index**: (ln(GNI per capita) - ln(Minimum value)) / (ln(Maximum value) - ln(Minimum value))
 
 
 
• The HDI is the geometric mean of normalized indices for each of the three dimensions.
 
• Countries are classified into four tiers of human development based on their HDI scores: **Very High Human Development, High Human Development, Medium Human Development, and Low Human Development.**
 
• The HDI has been widely used by policymakers and researchers to compare the level of human development across countries and to assess the impact of economic policies on people's well-being.

Percentage of students passed = 82% 

Percentage of students placed in reappear category = 2% 

Number of students failed = 592

Let the total number of students be 100% 

Percentage of students failed = 100% - Passed Percent - Reappear Category Percent 

⇒ 100% - 82% - 2% 

⇒ 16% 

∵ 16% = 592 

⇒ 100% = 592 × 100%/16%
